stories.headline: RealAssist turns client signals into reviewable agent actions

source.title: Realtor.com+ Unveils RealAssist AI for Agents to Power a More Intelligent Workspace

stories.summary: Realtor.com+ introduced RealAssist as an AI workspace for real-estate agents. It combines client activity into a daily digest and can recommend or prepare follow-up actions such as refined searches and drafted messages, while keeping the agent in the approval loop before anything is sent or acted on.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a practical pattern for nontechnical agent use: AI gathers scattered signals, proposes a next step, and hands the consequential decision back to the professional. The value comes from reducing coordination work without silently transferring authority.
stories.related_coverage: The Windows story shows a broader operating-system layer for delegated actions; RealAssist shows the same delegation pattern inside a specific profession.
stories.image_alt_intent: Mechanism diagram showing client signals entering a digest, proposed actions, explicit agent review, approved execution, and feedback returning to the next cycle.

stories.headline: Windows adds a containment layer for local and cloud AI actions
stories.summary: Microsoft is positioning Windows as a hybrid-intelligence layer that can route AI work between local and cloud resources. Microsoft Execution Containers are generally available on Windows 11 to isolate agent activity with file and network boundaries, while broader Copilot abilities to use local PC context and act on a user’s behalf are described as capabilities that will expand over time.
stories.why_it_matters: Desktop agents become more useful when they can see relevant local context, but that same access raises the cost of mistakes. Treating isolation, identity, permissions, and routing as platform primitives makes delegated computer use easier to constrain and audit.
stories.related_coverage: RealAssist illustrates review-before-action inside one profession; Windows addresses the operating-system boundary beneath more general delegated work.
stories.image_alt_intent: Layered system diagram showing user intent, local context, policy and identity, local-versus-cloud routing, an execution container, and a bounded action result.

stories.headline: Webex brings digital teammates into shared collaboration context
stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers

source.title: Cisco Unveils New Agentic Collaboration Experiences

stories.summary: Cisco announced new Webex experiences built around digital teammates that can participate in spaces, meetings, and calls with shared team context. Examples include one agent gathering analytics while another updates a presentation, with identity, security, AI Defense guardrails, and Splunk telemetry around the workflow. Several capabilities are described as upcoming rather than universally available today.
stories.why_it_matters: Knowledge work rarely happens in a single prompt. Agents that can enter the same conversational context as a team, coordinate specialized steps, and remain visible to governance systems point toward AI that participates in ongoing work instead of sitting beside it.
stories.related_coverage: The Google Developer Knowledge skill story packages specialist retrieval behavior for one agent; Webex shows multiple agents operating inside a shared team context.
stories.image_alt_intent: Hub-and-spoke mechanism showing shared team context connecting people, analytics and presentation agents, enterprise systems, governance controls, and reviewed actions.

stories.headline: Jump Trading scales long-horizon research without removing human acceptance
stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers

source.title: How Jump Trading is scaling quant research with ChatGPT

stories.summary: Jump Trading describes using GPT-6 Astra for longer, ambiguous research tasks by defining the problem, the working environment, and how output quality and significance will be evaluated. Agents can work for extended periods and be redirected, while consequential outputs such as trading signals remain subject to controlled human review.
stories.why_it_matters: Long-running research agents are most credible when autonomy is paired with explicit evaluation and an acceptance boundary. The pattern is useful well beyond quantitative finance: specify the environment, observe the work, evaluate evidence, and keep the final judgment with a responsible human.
stories.related_coverage: RealAssist uses approval before operational actions; Jump applies the same principle to open-ended research where the output may be informative but wrong.
stories.image_alt_intent: State-machine diagram showing research question, bounded environment, agent exploration, evidence evaluation, human acceptance, and controlled use of results with a return path for redirection.

stories.headline: Google packages fresh developer documentation as a reusable agent skill

source.title: Supercharge your development with the Google Developer Knowledge API ecosystem

stories.summary: Google introduced a Developer Knowledge API ecosystem that exposes current technical documentation as fresh Markdown and includes a reusable skill for compatible coding agents. The skill uses a multi-step retrieval pattern—searching for relevant snippets before pulling fuller documentation—and can connect through MCP across several agent environments.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a genuine reusable Agent Skill: durable retrieval behavior can be installed once and invoked across supported assistants instead of being reconstructed in every prompt. It also demonstrates why retrieval policy is part of skill design, not just a back-end detail.
stories.related_coverage: GitHub’s agent-scale infrastructure story addresses what happens when many coding agents act concurrently; this story addresses how an individual coding agent acquires current, authoritative context.
stories.image_alt_intent: Pipeline diagram showing developer intent entering a reusable skill, snippet search, relevance selection, fresh documentation retrieval, context assembly, and a grounded answer.

stories.headline: GitHub separates durable storage from compute for agent-scale Git traffic

source.title: Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development

stories.summary: GitHub says agentic development is sharply increasing pushes, branch activity, merge-queue pressure, and CI read fan-out. Its evolving Git architecture separates durable authoritative repository data in blob storage from lightweight compute and cache workers so read and write capacity can scale more independently while preserving branch protections, auditability, and review controls.
stories.why_it_matters: Agentic coding changes infrastructure economics because one human request can trigger many machine-speed repository operations. Systems designed for human-paced Git traffic need different storage, concurrency, and cache boundaries when agents continuously create, revise, and validate work.
stories.related_coverage: The Google Agent Skill story focuses on grounded coding behavior; GitHub’s architecture shows the repository substrate required when those agents operate at scale.
stories.image_alt_intent: Comparison diagram contrasting tightly coupled Git storage and compute with a decoupled architecture of authoritative blob storage, stateless workers, caches, refs, and CI fan-out.

videos.title: BigQuery Graph measures explained (Why your AI agents get metrics wrong and how measures fix it)
videos.summary: An 8:48 walkthrough of BigQuery Graph measures that shows why ordinary joins can double-count metrics and how reusable measures can give agentic analytics a more trustworthy semantic layer.
videos.why_it_matters: Agents that query business data need metric definitions that survive changing groupings and relationships; otherwise fluent answers can still return the wrong number.

videos.title: How to build an agentic C-Suite with Google Cloud ADK and Cloud Run
videos.summary: A 6:26 end-to-end demonstration of specialized agents passing context through decision loops and running as an application on Cloud Run.
videos.why_it_matters: The short build makes multi-agent orchestration concrete: split responsibilities, pass context deliberately, and keep the workflow inspectable rather than treating 'multi-agent' as a label.

podcasts.title: AI at work
podcasts.summary: Carmel Crimmins speaks with ADP chief economist Nela Richardson about how AI is changing tasks inside jobs, why career-stage effects differ, and why experience may remain more resilient than simple automation narratives suggest.
podcasts.why_it_matters: The episode grounds workplace-AI discussion in labor-market evidence rather than only product launches, helping readers separate task change from claims about wholesale job replacement.

podcasts.title: The New, New Kingmakers: Agents, Developers, and the Future of Software with Stephen O'Grady
podcasts.summary: Brandon Whichard interviews RedMonk co-founder Stephen O'Grady about how software developers gained influence over technology choices and how coding agents may now reshape that relationship between developers, platforms, and software creation.
podcasts.why_it_matters: It provides a useful strategic lens for the GitHub infrastructure story: agentic development changes not only coding speed but also who or what drives tool selection, workflow design, and software demand.

new.why: GitHub’s measured rise in pushes, refs pressure, and CI fan-out shows that agentic development is becoming an infrastructure problem, not only a coding-interface feature.
RealAssist makes a useful adoption pattern visible: AI can aggregate signals and prepare actions while the professional retains explicit approval over consequential outreach.

updated.what_changed: Google now ships a reusable Developer Knowledge skill that packages a retrieval policy around current official documentation and can be loaded into multiple compatible coding-agent environments.

updated.topic: Enterprise context becomes the agent battleground
updated.what_changed: Cisco is moving shared team context into collaborative agents, while Windows is making local context and containment part of the operating-system layer. Context is becoming an execution boundary as well as a retrieval problem.

carried_forward.why: Jump Trading’s research workflow, RealAssist’s approval boundary, Cisco governance controls, and Windows containment all reinforce the same pattern: broader agent authority needs explicit evaluation, identity, and review.
Cisco’s digital teammates and Windows’ expanding agent surface continue the shift from isolated prompt sessions toward assistants that participate in ongoing work and shared context.

book_mappings.concept_or_chapter: Human approval, decision boundaries, and acceptance criteria
book_mappings.connection: RealAssist shows a reliability pattern in which AI can prepare consequential work but the professional remains the acceptance gate before an external action occurs.
book_mappings.what_to_study_next: Study how to define which actions may be proposed automatically, which require review, and what evidence the reviewer should see.

book_mappings.concept_or_chapter: Permission-aware context, isolation, and execution boundaries
book_mappings.connection: Local context is useful only when retrieval and action are constrained by identity, permissions, routing, and containment. Windows makes those boundaries part of the platform architecture.
book_mappings.what_to_study_next: Study how context selection and tool permissions should change when an assistant can act on local files, apps, and network resources.

book_mappings.book: Generative AI Prompt Engineering Learning Ecosystem
book_mappings.concept_or_chapter: Shared context, feedback loops, and collaborative learning surfaces
book_mappings.connection: Agents participating inside team spaces create a recurring learning surface where context, human corrections, decisions, and outcomes can improve future delegated work.
book_mappings.what_to_study_next: Study how to preserve useful team context without turning every conversation into permanent memory or silently expanding an agent’s authority.

book_mappings.concept_or_chapter: Evaluation under uncertainty and responsible human acceptance
book_mappings.connection: Long-horizon research becomes more reliable when the task environment, success criteria, observability, and human acceptance boundary are explicit before the agent begins.
book_mappings.what_to_study_next: Study how to evaluate research outputs for quality and significance when a plausible answer may still be wrong.

book_mappings.book: Generative AI Professional Prompt Engineering Guide
book_mappings.concept_or_chapter: Reusable instructions, retrieval policy, and bounded specialist behavior
book_mappings.connection: Google’s Developer Knowledge skill packages a durable search-and-retrieve method that can be installed across compatible agents rather than repeated in task-specific prompts.
book_mappings.what_to_study_next: Study how reusable skill instructions should separate search strategy, authoritative-source selection, tool use, and task-specific user intent.

book_mappings.concept_or_chapter: System architecture for concurrent agent state and evidence
book_mappings.connection: As agents create many simultaneous repository operations, reliable context depends on durable authoritative state, scalable read paths, and clear separation between source-of-truth data and disposable compute caches.
book_mappings.what_to_study_next: Study how authoritative state, cache layers, provenance, and concurrency controls affect the context an agent sees during fast-changing work.
